name: php-inclusion-include-execute
rce_class: File inclusion reaching execution (bare include sink)
notes: The second half of what `php-inclusion-file-read` measures on the same
build, and it exists because that case's own notes were wrong about this
target. They said execution was out of reach here and the route that
works on a released build is two-step -- poison a log, then include it.
The first part was right about the reason and wrong about the
conclusion: allow_url_include is off, so no wrapper can carry code, but
a one-step route survives that setting. Make the sink include PEAR's own
command-line script and hand that script arguments through the query
string: `config-create` writes its output to a path the arguments name,
and the code goes in the output. Measured here, not reasoned about.
What distinguishes this case from `thinkphp-lang-include-execute` is one
character, and it is a property of the sink rather than of the target.
This sink is `include $_GET['file'];`, which opens exactly the path it is
given; PHP appends nothing. So the traversal has to name `pearcmd.php`
itself. ThinkPHP's language loader builds its own filename and appends
`.php`, so the path it is handed must NOT carry one. The corpus declares
both shapes, both are sent, and at most one can confirm on a given sink:
measured, this build confirms on `php_pearcmd_config_create_with_extension`
and reports `negative` on the extensionless sibling, while lang-rce does
the reverse. Without the pair, RCEKit reported a clean `negative` on a
sink it reaches -- which is the false negative this case pins.
This target is also the one that shows the per-depth proof is per depth.
The web root is /var/www/html, so every climb of three or more reaches /
and all three quick depths confirm -- measured, `executed=3` with three
distinct filenames and three distinct products. lang-rce confirms on one
depth only, the deepest, and the working depth there is the LAST probe
sent. That ordering is why the shared-filename defect this case was
written alongside was invisible on lang-rce and visible here: when the
first depth writes, every later depth could read its file back and claim
it. Each probe now carries its own filename and its own operands, so a
depth whose include failed reads a path nothing wrote and reports
`negative` rather than another depth's success.
The control is a tier ceiling and it removes the one thing the proof
rests on, keeping everything else: the same vulnerable build, the same
risk tier, the same probes, with no --include-write-url. The verdict here
comes from fetching the written file back, so with nowhere to read it
from this method must not reach `executed` on a target where it
otherwise does.
`--methods reflected` is NOT the control, although it is the control the
read case uses on this same sink and reports 19 clean negatives. It
cannot be used here: this invocation needs --verify-url-location raw, so
the payload is the whole query string, and a shell payload sent raw into
a query string breaks the request before it arrives. A control whose
probes mostly never reach the target says nothing about false
confirmation, which is why the runner refuses `error` as an expectation
at all. The claim that no shell method reaches this sink is already
pinned by the read case, where the delivery permits it.
